source_review.notes: Checked current primary Linux kernel documentation for memory concepts, page tables, memory APIs, and userfaultfd; current Linux man-pages for userfaultfd, mmap, madvise, mincore, and mlock; and MIT's 2025 xv6 text. All 10 cited URLs returned HTTP 200; Linux-specific accounting and interfaces, general demand-paging mechanisms, empirical performance, and assurance claims are distinguished.

evidence: Checked page and generation state S(v,g), demanded set D, populated set P, resident set R, fault count F, total fault time T_f, demanded bytes B_d, readahead bytes B_r, and useful bytes B_u.
Reviewed demand paging, resident page, anonymous and file-backed page, minor and major fault, readahead, page cache, first touch, prefault, residency, overcommit, and userfault terminology.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation separates state-machine identity, time-varying demand and residence, fault totals, and speculative-I/O usefulness.

evidence: Executed touches 0,3,3,9,15 within a sixteen-page reservation and confirmed four distinct first-touch faults.
Confirmed resident indices 0,3,9,15 and twelve untouched reserved pages.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The deterministic model omits frames, zeroing, mappings, I/O, concurrent faults, eviction, pressure, errors, and timing.

evidence: Re-derived publication eligibility from equality of current mapping generation and backing identity with the fault's captured state.
